guide.p: Choose a topic, set a timer and answer aloud. For Part 1 aim for 15–25 seconds per answer, for Part 2 one minute of notes and two minutes of talk, and for Part 3 around 40–60 seconds per answer. Record yourself and compare with the self-check criteria.

bullets: Do you live in a house or a flat?
Which room do you spend the most time in?
What would you change about your home?
Would you like to live somewhere else in the future?
What do you study / what is your job?
Why did you choose it?
What is the most enjoyable part of your day?
What would you like to do after you finish your studies?
What do you enjoy doing in your free time?
Did you have the same hobbies as a child?
Do you prefer spending free time alone or with others?
Is there a hobby you would like to try?
How often do you use your phone each day?
What apps do you use the most?
Is there any technology you could not live without?
Do you think you spend too much time online?
How do you usually travel around your city?
Do you prefer travelling by train or by car?
Where did you go on your last holiday?
Is public transport good where you live?

guide.h: Part 1 — Food, shopping, music and sport

bullets: What is a typical meal in your country?
Do you prefer shopping online or in shops?
What kind of music do you listen to when you want to relax?
Did you play any sports at school?
Do you enjoy watching sport on television?
Describe a teacher who influenced you. (who, what subject, what they were like, and explain why they influenced you)
Describe a journey you remember well. (where, who with, what happened, and explain why it was memorable)
Describe something you bought that you were pleased with. (what, where, how much, and explain why you liked it)
Describe a time you helped someone. (who, what you did, how they felt, and explain why you helped)
Describe an app or website you find useful. (what it is, how you found it, how you use it, and explain why it is useful)
Describe a festival or celebration in your country. (when, what people do, what you do, and explain why it is important)
Describe a goal you hope to achieve in the future. (what, when, how you will achieve it, and explain why it matters to you)
Describe a piece of advice you received. (who gave it, when, what it was, and explain how it helped you)
Describe a building you find interesting. (where, what it looks like, what it is used for, and explain why you find it interesting)
Describe a time you were very busy. (when, what you had to do, how you managed, and explain how you felt)
What makes a good teacher?
Is it better to study at university or to start work after school?
How has education in your country changed in recent years?
Should education be free at every level?
Who is more responsible for protecting the environment: governments or individuals?
Why do some people not recycle?
How could cities be made greener?
Will people travel by plane less in the future?
Has technology made people more or less sociable?
Should children have smartphones?
What jobs might disappear because of technology?
Do older people find it hard to keep up with technology? Why?
What is more important in a job: salary or satisfaction?
Why do some people change careers?
Is working from home good for society?
How will workplaces be different in twenty years?
What are the advantages of living in a big city?
Why do young people move away from villages?
How can neighbours build a stronger community?
What should governments do to make housing more affordable?
Why is it important to keep traditional festivals?
How has globalisation affected local culture?
Should museums be free to visit?
Do young people value tradition less than older people do?

guide.tip: Part 3 questions follow the Part 2 topic, so practise them as a set: one Part 2 card, then four related Part 3 questions.
